key_insight: Multilingual text embeddings from frozen LLMs are not naturally aligned across languages: semantically equivalent sentences can land in different regions of embedding space. The paper shows that removing paired language-specific residual subspaces can improve cross-lingual alignment without additional training.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the lack of effective training-free multilingual text embeddings for frozen LLMs. Existing methods work mainly in English and fail to capture language-invariant semantics across different languages.
method: Systematically analyze multilingual embedding geometry in frozen LLMs to identify language-conditioned misalignment.
Estimate language-specific residual subspaces using paired sentence representations across languages.
Remove these residual components to steer embeddings toward a more language-agnostic semantic space.
impact: This matters for practitioners building multilingual retrieval, clustering, and semantic search systems because it offers a training-free way to improve cross-language consistency. It can reduce reliance on costly multilingual fine-tuning while making frozen LLM embeddings more usable in real-world global applications.

paper_title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
paper_authors: Ailiang Lin, Zhuoyun Li, Yusong Wang, Keyu Mao, Kotaro Funakoshi
